Women: Sons serves no women. The hair flow stops at question 2 (re-tested live), the beard flow dead-ends (re-tested live), no product page or sitemap entry is for women, and the medical FAQ says Sons may not sell its 5% minoxidil to women. The women's route is therefore covered as a stop, not a flow.
Evidence labels: scripts/verify-labels.js checks that every 'observed' rule, question and option names a run folder that exists. After the corrections below it reports no gaps.

Partner-clinic route walked live for the first time (runs/verify-clinic-1, -2, -future, -future-continue, -past): treatment type, procedure date, a free post-op pack offer only for a date within the next two months, then an account form before any medical question (new rules R44 and R45).
Replays in stage 3: 12 by the earlier interrupted attempt (11 usable, one cut off) and 8 in this attempt, 20 in all, one at a time.
stillUnverified: Every product effect (R12 to R35): read and run offline from the code the site serves, and that code is confirmed unchanged today, but no recommendation page was ever seen live because it sits behind the account form.
Which of the two code copies new customers actually see, and whether the server overrides either (plan name in the sign-up reply, account/recommendations list, account tags).
The over-65 rule (R29) and the under-18 refusal (R30): both depend on the date of birth typed into the account form, which was never filled in.
What the prescriber does with red flags (sudden onset, PHQ-2 answers, scalp sores, psoriasis 'not willing to proceed') and how often orders are refused.
The clinic route after the account form (pre, post and free consultations, clinic recommendation page): code only.

Legal class (P or GSL) of the minoxidil 5% spray and ketoconazole shampoo. A web search found a UK public assessment report for minoxidil 5% cutaneous solution, PL 50640/0001, held by Careforsons and granted 6 Aug 2020, but no source stating its UK supply category; the Irish twin is not subject to prescription. Not opened directly, so left unconfirmed.
Topical strengths (finasteride 0.15%, combination spray 0.15% / 5% / tretinoin 0.015%, dutasteride 0.1%) come from the served dose table and leaflets; the live product pages do not print them.
verdict: The questionnaire side of this report is trustworthy. Every stop, branch and extra screen that matters was replayed live at least once, the baselines replay identically a day later, and the survey definition is unchanged. The product side is trustworthy as code, not as observed fact: the rules that remove a drug family (sudden onset, PHQ-2, side effects, heart and blood pressure, finasteride exclusions, scalp disorder, lactose, over 65) match both copies of the served code line for line, both copies are still served byte-for-byte unchanged, and an independent offline re-run gives the stated plans. But no recommendation was seen live, the server can override the browser, and the prescriber's decisions are unknown, so these rules show what the site is built to offer, not what a patient finally receives. Stage 3 found no contradicted product rule. It corrected proof that pointed at a missing run folder, unlabelled 'observed' claims, an inaccurate 'silent' dead end in the beard flow, a beard warning that turned out to have no effect, and an untested partner-clinic route that asks for an account before any medical question. Prices and actives checked against 14 live product pages all matched.

access.coverageNote: Stage 1 walked the baseline man to the account form and saw every conditional screen. Stage 2 replayed both baselines and then 45 one-change experiments live, each ending on the account form, the female stop notice or the sign-in page. Because no plan is shown before the account form, product effects could not be seen live: instead both copies of the recommendation code that the site serves to every visitor were run offline on the same one-change answers (28 further offline-only cases, plus all 32,768 combinations of the answers the code reads). Stage 3 (24 Nov 2026) replayed the baselines and the stop rules again (20 live replays in all), walked the partner-clinic route to its account form, confirmed that the survey definition and both copies of the recommendation code are unchanged, re-ran the newer code offline, and checked 14 live product pages and the product sitemap. Nothing behind an account form was tested: no account, email, phone number, date of birth, photo, payment or order was entered or created.
access.accountWall: Hair and beard flows: after the last consent screen (finasteride statement in the hair flow). The next screen is an account form (first name, last name, email, phone, date of birth, password) titled "Based on your questionnaire results, we are now preparing your personalised health plan. Please complete your account set up to continue." No recommendation, product or price is shown before it. Pressing "Get my personalised plan" creates the account and sends the consultation together. Answering "Yes" to "Are you an existing Sons customer?" hits the sign-in page at question 1. Partner-clinic pages: the account form ("Create your account") comes straight after treatment type and procedure date, before any medical question.

limitationsAdd: Stage 3 walked the partner-clinic route only to its account form, for one clinic (British Hair Clinic); other clinics may differ.

engineSummaryAdd: Partner transplant-clinic pages work differently: they ask only the treatment type and procedure date, offer a free post-op pack when the procedure is within the next two months, and ask for an account before any medical question (seen live in stage 3).
